content: I've confirmed this is a kernel soundness bug who can @Gershon Bialer share this with privately?
This will not pass lake comparator, thus it is not a soundness bug. Please review https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/ValidatingProofs.

If I understand the situation, then the idea of the exploit is to have a prelude definition (autoParam) that the C++ kernel assumes to be exactly as in the official prelude, and give it a different definition.

This means it is really a rerun of the familiar “fake prelude confuses the kernel” story, a show usually staged with Nat.add or so.

This is documented behavoiur: If you feed non-standard prelude definitions to the kernel all bets are off. That is why comparator has a list of constants that it always includes in the challenge export (primitiveTargets in src/lake/Lake/CLI/Check.lean).

Furthermore, there is the additional protection you get form using other checkers. Especially the verified and soon-verified ones (lean4lean, con-leche, con-ron) validate such prelude definitions.

TL;DR: Nothing to see, carry on.

(Still thanks to Gershon for trying to find and report soundness isuses; if there was one we’d want to know about it!)

If you import autoParam definition to the challenge statement, you can prove arbitrary statements in comparator. Comparator compares the definitions between the challenge and proof.

If you are using standard challenge statements, it won't work. Some alternative checkers do catch the issue.

MinPoisonPass.tar.gz
Here it passes comparator if you import environment into the challenge statement.

Right, that’s also working as intended: The Challenge is trusted. This is not much different from a challenge that includes nonstandard axioms, or misleading syntax.

This is why it's important to review challenges for shenanigans, and also why we have trusted places for vetted challenges (https://google-deepmind.github.io/formal-conjectures/).

Proposal: since we have the comparator framework ready, we can tell people that to report a soundness bug, they should (privately) submit a proof of False somewhere. It's trivial to vet a challenge of False.

(If reports are rare enough then this doesn't matter.)

https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/new?template=bug_report.md now says

When reporting a perceived soundness bug: Does it affect lake check --paranoid? If in doubt, please reach out on security@lean-fro.org for responsible disclosure.
